packageRules.description: One branch per ecosystem rather than one for the whole fleet. A failing check then parks only the ecosystem it belongs to, and a revert names what broke. Grouping by manager also subsumes the monorepo presets that the base configuration brings, because a monorepo's packages all share one ecosystem; those presets are left to decide major, which is where a coordinated bump actually matters
Workflow actions move on their own cadence and break the pipeline rather than the product, so they are worth reading apart from application dependencies
A base image carries an operating system, not a library, so its blast radius is the runtime rather than the call graph

Every Python manager is named rather than matched on a category, because extraction happens before categories are known and the fleet mixes pyproject, requirements and setup.cfg in the same repository
Toolchain pins decide what a contributor's machine runs, not what the product ships, so they are their own branch

This preset's own pin in a consuming repository. The quarantine is cleared because the change was reviewed and validated here before it was tagged, and a week of ageing would make every fleet-wide fix arrive a week late. The package is named because the manager tracks any preset that names a tag, a third party's included, and that one was reviewed nowhere here, so it keeps the quarantine like any other dependency. WARNING: the manager only sees a preset that names a tag, so a repository extending the bare branch gets no pull request and silently tracks master instead

A language runtime is pinned in several files at once — the go directive and the golang image, a setup action's input, a version file, a toolchain manager — and each would otherwise raise a branch of its own. Grouping it by name across managers moves every pin in one commit, so a build never mixes two versions of the same runtime. Majors still split off into a branch of their own, because separateMajorMinor applies inside a group

Digest and pin moves keep the tag, so they are a rebuilt layer rather than an upgrade decision and belong in one branch of their own. The ageing requirement is cleared here deliberately: a digest carries no release timestamp to age against, and minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour: timestamp-required would otherwise hold every one of them indefinitely

A digest move under a tag that names no version — latest, alpine, stable — is not a rebuilt layer but whatever upstream released since, majors and schema migrations included, and it arrives with no quarantine because digests are exempt from one. It is therefore a decision. The durable answer is a versioned tag in the consuming repository, which turns the same move into an ordinary update with a type and an age. It leaves the digest group for the reason the pre-1.0 rule gives

A pre-1.0 package may break on a minor and semver permits it, so it leaves the automerging group into one of its own. WARNING: it must leave rather than merely lose automerge, because a branch automerges only when every upgrade in it does, so a single pre-1.0 member would park the whole group. The excluded packages are permanently 0.x by convention and versioned with the stability of a 1.x: the Go extended library, the generated Google API stubs and the OpenTelemetry contrib modules that move in lockstep with their 1.x core. Without the exclusion every one of them, security fixes included, waits for a decision

Below 0.1 semver gives no compatibility promise at all, so even a patch may break, and packages that live there for years ship their breaking changes exactly that way. It joins the pre-1.0 branch rather than starting another

A major upgrade is a decision, not a refresh, so it opens a pull request straight away, assigned and with the checks already run, and waits there for the merge button; it is never folded into an ecosystem group. The longer quarantine is the same reasoning applied to time: a major carries the breaking change by definition, so it gets the far end of the window rather than the near one. The managers excluded here are decided by the rules below instead; they are excluded rather than overridden because addLabels accumulates and a branch cannot usefully carry both needs-decision and automerge

The same decision for npm and pyproject, which are held out of the rule above so that development dependencies can be told apart. WARNING: the type is negated rather than listed, because npm also extracts engines, packageManager, volta, overrides and resolutions, and pyproject extracts requires-python and build-system.requires; a positive list of runtime types would drop those out of every major rule and leave them automerging on the inherited default

A major in the development toolchain breaks the pipeline rather than the product, and breaks it inside its own pull request, where a red check holds the merge and assigns it without anybody being asked in advance. Base images are deliberately not here: a major there is a change of operating system, which passes the checks and shows up in production. Language runtimes are not here either, although these managers extract them, because the runtime a setup action or a toolchain file installs is the one the product is built and tested on

Linters, formatters, test runners and type stubs are not shipped, so their majors are answered by the build. A package that a repository keeps among its runtime dependencies rather than its development ones is not covered and still asks, which is the right way round
The runtime majors the toolchain rule leaves out, decided like any other major

Python versions its language on the minor: 3.13 to 3.14 removes deprecated modules, changes the ABI that compiled wheels target and is where packages drop support, so it is a major in everything but name. It leaves the runtime group for the reason the pre-1.0 rule gives

A major of this preset is still a decision, because it is what a consuming repository has to act on, but it is not a third party's breaking change, so it skips the quarantine for the reason the rule for its minors gives. Only the age is cleared: the major rules above still withhold automerge and label it. WARNING: it must stay below every rule that sets the fourteen days, because the last matching rule decides minimumReleaseAge

Anything that will merge itself says so on its pull request. Assignees are withheld from these by assignAutomerge: a pull request that merges itself needs no owner, and Renovate assigns one only when the checks go red, which is exactly when an owner is needed
Minor is qualified because the pre-1.0 and python runtime rules above withhold automerge from it
The permanently 0.x packages the pre-1.0 rules exclude automerge, so they carry the label the two rules above withhold from 0.x
Digest is qualified because the unversioned tag rule above withholds automerge from a docker digest whose tag names no version
